+1, I’m seeing the same class of bug on v1.2.10 with Anthropic/Claude flows.
In my repo, the real path is `/home/<user>/working/opencode-review`, but Claude-facing env context has reported `/home/<user>/working/Claude-review` (non-existent). This then cascades into wrong artifact paths like `docs/Claude/...` instead of `docs/opencode/...`.
Key point: opencode session/project metadata on disk still shows the correct directory (`.../opencode-review`), so this looks like a runtime prompt/context injection rewrite issue in the Claude path, not a local repo/config misconfiguration.
Here is an example repo where the issue occurs: https://github.com/wetlandscapes/agentic-code-review/tree/main.

Hi! Quick update from my side: I built and published a plugin that works around the GLM clipboard image issue in OpenCode.

It keeps the same paste UX (Cmd+V / clipboard image) for GLM models by:
- detecting pasted data:image/... parts,
- writing the image to a temp local file,
- replacing the image part with a text instruction that includes the local file path so image MCP tools can process it. 
- It also includes automatic temp cleanup.

Plugin:
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/opencode-glm-clipboard
- repo: https://github.com/WilfredLemus/opencode-glm-clipboard

Install:
npx -y opencode-glm-clipboard@latest

> This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:

> * [[FEATURE]: Introduce ordered list for model options #13977](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/13977): Proposes similar model grouping/tiering with provider fallback lists (e.g. defining an ordered list of models per agent, trying the first available and falling back to the next)

Thanks — I reviewed #13977 and I think my request is **related but not a duplicate**.

### Key difference: **system-level model identity & provider routing**, not project/agent-level lists
- **#13977**: focuses on configuring an **ordered list of model options per agent/project** (i.e., the agent tries model A, then model B, etc.). This is primarily **per-project / per-agent configuration** of alternatives.
- **My request**: focuses on **global (system-level) deduplication and management of the *same underlying model* across multiple providers**.

### What I’m asking for (system-level)
1. **Merge/Deduplicate identical models across providers** into a single “model identity” (alias/group) at the **global config / system** layer.
   - Example: “Opus 4.6” appears from:
     - Claude Subscription Pro
     - GitHub Copilot
     - API Provider(s)
   - These should be **one merged model entry** in UI/config, not multiple duplicates.

2. For that merged model identity, support a **global provider priority order**:
   - Claude Subscription Pro → GitHub Copilot → API Provider(s)

3. When quota is exhausted / rate-limited / provider unavailable, OpenCode should **seamlessly fail over** to the next provider **for the same model**, without the user having to change model selection.
   - This is **provider-level failover within the same model**, not “try a different model”.

### Why system-level matters
- It simplifies the model list and avoids repetitive duplicates across projects.
- It enables cost/quota optimization globally (“use subscription quota first, then copilot, then API”).
- Projects/agents can still select the merged model identity, while routing is handled centrally.

### Relationship to #13977
I see #13977 as potentially complementary:
- #13977 could be used for **project-level preference between different models** (e.g., Opus vs Sonnet vs GPT).
- My request is for **system-level identity & provider routing for the same model** (Opus across providers), which reduces duplication and improves reliability.

If maintainers agree, I’m happy to reword this issue title/description to make the scope distinction clearer (system/global vs project/agent).

**Reviewer's guide** — supplementary context not covered in the PR description. Uses same terminology (S1/S2, M1/M2) defined there.

---

### AI SDK cache marker mechanics

Ref: [Anthropic prompt caching docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching) | Anthropic engineers' caching best practices (Feb 19 2026): [Thariq Shihipar](https://x.com/trq212/status/2024574133011673516?s=20), [R. Lance Martin](https://x.com/RLanceMartin/status/2024573404888911886?s=20)

Max 4 `cache_control` markers per request. The AI SDK already places markers on the first 2 system blocks and the last 2 conversation turns. That part works — the problem is OpenCode mutating blocks *before* these markers, cascading hash changes downstream.

Key subtlety: before this PR, OpenCode had a single system block. M1 covered it, but M2 was unused — it fell through to conversation. The system split (commit 3) is what activates both markers, letting S1 (stable) cache independently from S2 (dynamic).

Since M1 covers the tool block too (tools hash before system in Anthropic's ordering), any tool instability (commits 4–5) completely invalidates M1 — the entire cached prefix up to that marker is lost.

### Related open PRs

Several open PRs address parts of this (#5422, #14203, #10380, #11492). This PR addresses the root causes directly.

### Update (post-rebase, Mar 21 2026)

- Skill ordering commit dropped (covered by #18261)
- Global skills now placed in S1 (stable block) alongside provider prompt and global AGENTS.md. Project skills remain in S2. This was needed because #18261 added `SystemPrompt.skills()` to the system prompt during the rebase.
- Added `splitSystemPrompt` provider option (default: on). Providers that reject multiple system messages can set `splitSystemPrompt: false` in their provider config to get single-block behavior.

Im getting the same problem. Opus 4.5 works just fine, but 4.6 wont. So I started investigating (with opus 4.6 in chat mode) Maybe this will help you guys: There it is. The JS bundle (v0.0.388) only knows claude-opus-4.5 — no claude-opus-4.6. The native binary (v0.0.414) supports it. The npm-loader tries the native binary first via spawnSync, but inside the sandbox, the native binary spawn likely fails on write permissions (for stdio/ptty), so it falls back to the old JS bundle. Component | Version | Has opus-4.6? -- | -- | -- Native binary (copilot-darwin-arm64) | 0.0.414 | ✅ Yes npm JS bundle (@github/copilot) | 0.0.388 | ❌ No The npm-loader tries the native binary first, but inside the sandbox, the spawnSync fails (likely write permission for stdio), so it falls back to the old JS bundle which doesn't know about claude-opus-4.6. Fix — update the npm package: `npm install -g @github/copilot@latest` Or alternatively, run with --no-sandbox to let the native binary work directly.

PR #14743 addresses the root causes of cache misses directly: system prompt split into stable/dynamic blocks, bash tool schema cwd removal, skill tool ordering stabilization, optional system prefix freeze, and optional 1h TTL. Cross-repo first-prompt hit rate goes from 0% → 97.6% in my setup (your numbers will differ based on your tool set and global AGENTS.md size, but the cross-repo miss is eliminated regardless).

PR #14743 fixes this — the environment block is now in a separate system block (block 2) from the stable provider prompt and global AGENTS.md (block 1). Block 1 caches independently across repos and sessions. Optionally, `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_CACHE_STABILIZATION=1` also freezes the date and instruction reads for the process lifetime, giving you full hits past S1 until you restart OpenCode.

PR #14743 addresses the root causes of Anthropic prefix cache misses: system prompt was a single merged block (dynamic content invalidated stable content), bash tool schema included the absolute cwd (changed per-repo), and skill tool ordering was nondeterministic. If you're on Anthropic, cross-repo first-prompt hit rate goes from 0% → 97.6% in my setup. The prefix stability fixes may also help providers with automatic prefix caching (OpenAI, DeepSeek, Gemini, etc.) but I can't confirm for DeepInfra specifically.

Quick research update after digging in locally:

I can reproduce this on current `dev`. `/doc` shows `GET /event` with only `directory`, while `GET /event?session=<id>` still returns `200` and opens SSE.

Root cause appears to be in `packages/opencode/src/server/server.ts`:
- query validation is defined as `z.object({ directory: z.string().optional() })`
- `/event` OpenAPI route metadata does not define a `session` parameter
- the handler uses `Bus.subscribeAll(...)` and does not read `session` from query

So `session` is effectively accepted/ignored at runtime, but not represented in the OpenAPI contract.

Plan:
1. add `session` to the `/event` OpenAPI query params,
2. align route query schema/behavior with intended `session` semantics,
3. add regression coverage for `/doc` and regenerate SDK artifacts if needed.

If this direction looks good, I’ll open a PR.
